data.name: Aniruddha
data.gender_notes: Aniruddha is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Aniruddha is a name derived from Sanskrit language. It is a name of Lord Krishna's grandson, Aniruddha, who is also known as the 'Lord of Aniruddha'. He is a significant character in the Indian epic Mahabharata. Aniruddha is considered to be an incarnation of Lord Vishnu, the preserver of the universe. The name Aniruddha carries the meaning “Lord of Aniruddha” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Aniruddha usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of aniruddha and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine grace and protection.
data.etymology: Aniruddha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Aniruddha.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aniruddha total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Aniruddha holds a significant cultural impact in Hindu mythology. He is a part of the Mahabharata, one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India. The name 'Aniruddha' is revered and celebrated in Hindu communities, particularly those following the devotional Bhakti tradition. The story of Aniruddha is recounted through various folktales, legends, and literature, underscoring his importance in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Aniruddha is a divine name deeply entwined with spiritual significance for Hindus. He represents a collapsible or indestructible form of God, symbolizing the timelessness and invincibility of the divine. Believers believe that observing rituals, mantras, and worship related to Aniruddha bestows protection, blessings, and spiritual growth. Furthermore, Aniruddha is considered to be a patron of true love and devotion. His name and story remind us of the eternal nature of divine existence and the importance of devotion in our spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Aniruddha: Unconquerable, ever dreaming in the divine womb of Vishnu, embodiment of supreme devotion.

historical_references.reference:
Aniruddha is the grandson of Krishna and the son of Prasenjit and Rukmini. He is also an avatar (incarnation) of Lord Vishnu. In the Mahabharata, Aniruddha is described as the most powerful and handsome among all the Yadavas.
Context: Hindu Mythology, Mahabharata.
Time_period: 3102-3062 BCE

Aniruddha also appears in the Bhagavata Purana as the son of Prasenjit and Rukmini. He is said to have been born to fulfill the prophecy that Rukmini would bear a son who would destroy the great demon Jalandhara.
Context: Hindu Mythology, Bhagavata Purana.
Time_period: 3214-3137 BCE
